The 1.21.10 port's tick_tracking (particles.rs:3888, the drain that moves every created particle from pending into the live list — create() pushes to pending, :2098) enforces the 26.2 form (:3933-3945): at 16,384 live particles every new particle is dropped, and above 12,288 new particles are dropped with probability 1 - ((16384-size)/4096)^2, drawing the level random for each rejection (constant at :1358-1359). The port's behaviour matches neither vanilla 1.21.10 (evict oldest) nor vanilla 26.1.2 (plain queue, no cap at all). The cap only bites in particle-heavy scenes (above 12,288 live particles); below that threshold the port matches vanilla exactly. The repair here is evict-oldest, not the 26.1 tree's cap removal.
